summary.headline: KIMS Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 35.3% YoY to INR 1,180 crore, with EBITDA pre-Ind AS at INR 222 crore and debt cut to INR 2,570 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total revenue of INR 1,196 crore (+36.1% YoY, +10.3% QoQ) and EBITDA of INR 240 crore at a 20.1% margin, with PAT of INR 37 crore versus INR 85 crore a year earlier. Growth was driven by IP volumes (+26.6% YoY) and OP volumes (+28.5% YoY), with the Kondapur hospital commissioned in June and Palakkad (Kerala) opened. The QIP raised INR 1,500 crore, of which INR 1,100-1,125 crore repaid debt, and a INR 600 crore promoter preferential allotment is partly pending. Management guided Telangana to 30-35% margins over time, Kerala to 20-22% in two to three years, and Bengaluru to break-even for the full year, while several new units are still ramping up.

financial_highlights.change: +20.1% YoY, +10.9% QoQ; margin vs 20.27% in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated EBITDA pre-Ind AS excluding other income

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 85 crore in Q1 FY26 and INR 33 crore in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR 2,570 crore as of 30 June 2026; about INR 2,400 crore after early July repayments

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and equivalents (incl. liquid MF and deposits <12m)

segments.name: Telangana cluster (incl. Kondapur, Secunderabad)
segments.commentary: Management said revenue and EBITDA grew strongly YoY in Telangana and Andhra; Kondapur did INR 45 crore in July (first full month) against INR 32-33 crore monthly previously. Telangana occupancy is about 61% on the adjusted bed base excluding Kondapur and 200 Secunderabad beds under renovation.

segments.name: Bengaluru cluster (Mahadevapura, Electronic City)
segments.commentary: Mahadevapura reached EBITDA break-even in June and did about INR 20 crore revenue in July; Electronic City expected to break even in about one to two quarters. Management aims for zero EBITDA for the cluster for FY27. Census-bed occupancy at Mahadevapura is about 40%.

segments.name: Maharashtra (Thane, Nashik, Nagpur)
segments.commentary: Thane averaged about INR 16 crore monthly revenue in Q1 and did INR 21 crore in July at about 10% EBITDA margin. Nashik reached EBITDA break-even in Q1; Nagpur did INR 30 crore revenue in July. Empanelment delays of four to five months weighed on Q1.

segments.name: Kerala
segments.commentary: Kerala margins are in the single digits currently, with management expecting mid-teens in FY28 and 20-22% over two to three years after a 4-5% entry-cost drag. Palakkad opened, taking Kerala to three units; one more hospital (Thrissur) is due in three to four months.

segments.name: Andhra Pradesh
segments.commentary: Management said AP remains strong. Q1 ARPOB growth slowed from prior quarters (Q4 FY26 about INR 27,000), which management attributed to seasonal case mix. Cancer services were added to most AP hospitals in the last two to three months.

guidance_outlook: Telangana EBITDA margin expected to return to 30-35% over time as new Kondapur and Secunderabad beds ramp up; management said 30% is achievable by FY30 without new beds, and 70% occupancy is targeted in three to four years.
Bengaluru cluster targeted at zero EBITDA for full FY27; Bengaluru ARPOB expected to settle at INR 80,000-85,000 once empanelments complete, versus about INR 90,000+ recently.
Kondapur full potential of about INR 100 crore revenue per month (about INR 1,200 crore a year) within four to five years; model margin around 30%, with 30-32% suggested for the next two years.
ARPOB growth guidance of 4-5% per year; management called 15-16% historical growth too aggressive to model.
Maintenance capex about INR 100 crore per year for three to four years; about INR 100-125 crore growth capex over the next nine months, including Rajahmundry construction (INR 60-75 crore in FY27).
Debt-equity intended to be kept around 2.5:1; surplus cash to go to greenfield and brownfield growth in core states. Minority interest about 10.5% currently, 10-15% longer term.
Empanelment with the remaining 50% of insurers, covering Thane, Nashik and two Bengaluru assets, expected by end-August to mid-September 2026.
capex_capacity: Kondapur hospital commissioned in June 2026 (first patient 20 June); about 450-500 operational beds added in the last 10 days of Q1, and the old Kondapur hospital will run for about six more months with rent of about INR 90 lakh per month plus GST and INR 3-4 crore a year of operating cost.

Palakkad (Kerala) opened in Q1; Thrissur to commence in three to four months; Electronic City and other Bengaluru beds added at Mahadevapura (operational beds up from about 170 to 210, total cluster 280 to 340).
Secunderabad: old 250-bed facility demolished; replacement facility expected by end of next year.

Two O&M agreements (Golden Lan Solutions, Sarvottam Healthcare) approved in draft: a 300-bed Telangana hospital near Kondapur with INR 90-95 crore monthly revenue potential, and a Kakinada hospital currently at INR 7-8 crore a month, targeting INR 15-20 crore. O&M means no losses borne by KIMS.
Future pipeline: greenfield in Karnataka (300-350 beds, expandable by about 100) and acquisitions in Maharashtra, Kerala, Telangana and Andhra; timing and bed count not committed.

qa_highlights.question: Kerala cost increase and steady-state margin, plus whether the Q1 ARPOB jump is structural or seasonal.
qa_highlights.answer: Kerala is in growth phase; single-digit EBITDA margin now, mid-teens next financial year, and 20-22% over two to three years after a 4-5% entry-cost drag. Management said ARPP is the better metric; ARPOB moves with seasonal case mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why Telangana occupancy sits around 50-52% and whether it can rise further.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bed count includes 250 demolished Secunderabad beds not yet operational; ex-Kondapur and ex-200 renovating beds occupancy is about 61%. 70% is achievable in three to four years without new beds.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost impact after the INR 1,100 crore debt repayment.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said QIP proceeds arrived around 24 June and debt was repaid on 27-28 June, so the interest saving was not in Q1 and will show from Q2. Debt was INR 2,570 crore at 30 June, about INR 2,400 crore after early July repayments.

qa_highlights.question: Kondapur losses, pre-operative costs and status of the old hospital.
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-operative costs about INR 1.5-2 crore a month; Q1 losses marginal. Old hospital runs about six more months at about INR 90 lakh a month rent plus GST and INR 3-4 crore a year operating cost.

qa_highlights.question: Thane ramp-up lagging peers and when it turns breakeven.
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q1 weakness to a four-to-five-month empanelment delay and seasonality. Thane averaged about INR 16 crore monthly in Q1 and did INR 21 crore in July at about 10% margin; a healthy margin is expected if the trend holds.

qa_highlights.question: Telangana margin: why 30% guidance versus historical 35% peaks.
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed 30-35% over time, citing FY25-26 margins of about 31%, Secunderabad at 34-35% and Q4 FY26 Telangana at 38-39%. Return to 30%-plus will take time as new beds ramp.

demand_pricing: IP volumes 72,493 (+26.6% YoY, +14% QoQ); OP volumes 6,58,617 (+28.5% YoY, +8% QoQ); management cited FY25-based annual growth of 15.4% for IP and 25.4% for OP.
Average revenue per operating bed +9.7% YoY and +0.1% QoQ; ARPP +6.8% YoY and -3.8% QoQ. Management said ARPP is the better indicator, as ARPOB moves with ALOS and seasonal case mix.

Kondapur commissioned with first patient on 20 June 2026; July (first full month) revenue about INR 45 crore versus INR 32-33 crore monthly previously. Management said Kondapur full potential is about INR 100 crore per month within four to five years.

Bengaluru ARPOB running at INR 90,000+ for two quarters; management guided INR 80,000-85,000 once empanelments complete, with ARPP said to be similar to Telangana. Mahadevapura census-bed occupancy about 40%.

Telangana occupancy about 61% excluding Kondapur and 200 Secunderabad beds under renovation; management targets 70% in three to four years without new beds, and said about 65% on a prior adjusted basis was also cited. ARPOB growth guided at 4-5% a year; management called 15-16% too aggressive.

Insurance empanelment: about 50% of insurers done; remaining 50% covering Thane, Nashik and two Bengaluru assets expected by end-August to mid-September 2026. Maharashtra Q1 hit by four-to-five-month empanelment delay; Thane July revenue INR 21 crore at about 10% EBITDA margin.
risks_watch: Empanelment: remaining 50% of insurers, covering Thane, Nashik and two Bengaluru assets, due by end-August to mid-September 2026; the Joint Insurance Committee common-empanelment process is unresolved.
Ramp-up of new units: Electronic City breakeven guided in one to two quarters; Thane margin and Kerala single-digit margins still weak.
Bengaluru ARPOB may fall from INR 90,000+ toward INR 80,000-85,000 as empanelments complete.
Telangana occupancy about 61% on the adjusted base; Secunderabad 250-bed replacement not due until end of next year, and the 200 renovating beds are excluded from the base.
Government receivables improving but not fully on time; management said loss funding dropped only a little in Q1.
Acquisitions and greenfield timing not committed; management declined to quantify bed additions for FY28-29 and said the O&M deals (Golden Lan, Sarvottam) are draft-stage.
key_quotes: The first month has been very promising. We grew by almost 40% in less than a month.
As far as Telangana is concerned, we do not see any reason why we cannot ramp up to 70%, in spite of the new Kondapur hospital and the new Secunderabad hospital over the next three to four years.
I think it is too aggressive. Four to five is a good number.
Most likely it will get invested for greenfield and brownfield growth.
summary.management_tone: Confident on cluster trajectories and Telangana margins, with management reiterating 30-35% over time and a 70% occupancy target. Cautious and non-committal on acquisition and greenfield timing, and on the ARPOB and empanelment outcomes, which it tied to uncontrolled external factors.
